label: Confirmed Deaths
source: Government/Defensoría del Pueblo tallies (as of Jul 9, 2026)
contestNote: Union and independent sources dispute how many deaths are directly attributable to blockade-caused hospital shortages (~14 of the total) versus other causes.

label: State of Emergency
deltaNote: Due to expire around Sep 18, 2026 (90 days from the Jun 20 declaration); cocalero federations aligned with Evo Morales have staged an armed vigil ahead of the expiry.

label: Active Blockades
deltaNote: San Julián and Cuatro Cañadas blockades were lifted Sept 3 after producers reached a deal with the government built around Decree 5698's expanded 2,500-liter subsidized-diesel allowance for small producers; Defense Minister Justiniano visited Cuatro Cañadas with YPFB technicians to explain the new mechanism. The Yapacaní blockade on the Cochabamba–Santa Cruz road continued as of Sept 3; Los Troncos's status was unconfirmed. Decree 5676's underlying Bs. 18/liter large-consumer tier remains unrepealed. Separately, thousands of cocaleros marched in defiance of the state of emergency in Cochabamba on Sept 4, demanding the decree's repeal, though without installing new roadblocks.

label: USD Exchange Rate (floated)
source: Central Bank of Bolivia (official TCO, Sep 4, 2026)
deltaNote: New record high under the floated regime, up from the 15-year peg of Bs. 6.96 before the Jun 29 float. After a late-July peak near Bs. 12.13, the official rate eased to ~Bs. 11.50-11.71 in mid-to-late August, ticked back up to Bs. 11.83-11.93 by Aug 28-29, surpassed its prior peak at Bs. 12.26 on Sep 2 amid the renewed Santa Cruz blockades and YPFB intervention, and climbed further to Bs. 12.45 by Sep 4.

label: Inflation (y/y)
contestNote: The IMF forecasts full-year 2026 inflation near 20.7%, but Bolivia's statistics institute (INE) reported an official year-on-year print of just 4.93% for July 2026 — pass-through from the June currency float and December fuel-subsidy cuts had not yet fully hit consumer prices.

label: Diesel Price — Large Consumers (GRACOS)
deltaNote: Up from the prior Bs. 9.80-9.90/L rate; the subsidized Bs. 9.80/L price is unchanged for transport operators and individual consumers
contestNote: Facing backlash over the 84% hike, Deputy Hydrocarbons Minister Hernán Paredes said Aug 25 the decree "has to be modified" toward a more competitive price. But Minister of the Presidency Fernando Aramayo rejected repeal on Aug 27, attributing the decree to IMF conditionality; new blockades against it began Aug 26 in Beni and Oruro. New Economy Minister Christian Morales Burgos, sworn in Aug 25 replacing interim minister Óscar Mario Justiniano, said Aug 26 the decree needs adjustments "to minimize risks" from producer mobilizations; the Pro Santa Cruz Civic Committee set a 72-hour ultimatum (deadline Sun Aug 30) to repeal it before escalating to a region-wide Asamblea de la Cruceñidad.

label: Arrests (crisis-related)
contestNote: MAS-aligned and union groups characterize a portion of arrests and the Evo Morales warrant as politically motivated prosecution.

label: Cerimedo-Linked Detentions
value: 4 held + 1 arrest ordered; Cerimedo under 2 preventive detention orders
deltaNote: Santa Cruz prosecutors ordered the arrest of María Argentina Rojas Roca, a former Viru Viru Customs chief with a prior drug-trafficking conviction, as an alleged coordinator/paymaster of the gunmen who shot Nadia Beller, Aug 31. Judge Douglas Borda had ordered a second six-month preventive detention against Cerimedo on Aug 29, this time for illicit enrichment, to be served at Chonchocoro prison in addition to his existing Palmasola detention over the attempted-femicide case; Cerimedo clashed with Vice President Edmand Lara, who took part in the hearing to request his transfer, calling Lara a "mythomaniac." Separately, Police Commander General Mirko Sokol resigned Aug 31 amid a related audio-leak probe into alleged payments to influence police promotions and his own removal; VP Lara filed a fresh criminal complaint Sept 1 against First Lady Urquidi and Cerimedo over Sokol's ouster, and released a second disputed audio Sept 3 alleging Paz and Cerimedo scripted a "narrative" for the state of exception.

label: YPFB State Intervention
source: Government of Bolivia, Supreme Decree 5697, Sep 2, 2026
deltaNote: President Paz placed state oil company YPFB under "extraordinary, transparent and temporary" intervention for up to 180 days (extendable once by 90), via a commission of the Economy, Production/Environment/Water, Hydrocarbons/Energy and Public Works ministries, to audit the fuel import/distribution chain and trace smuggling and diversion networks. The decree does not dissolve YPFB or change its legal status.
